title: Optimizing Inventory Lookup for Retail Logistics
business: A regional retail distribution center managing thousands of unique product SKUs.
problem: The center uses a flat list to track inventory, resulting in linear search times that delay order fulfillment as the product catalog grows.
solution: Implementing a Binary Search Tree (BST) organizes SKUs into a hierarchical structure where each node's left subtree contains smaller keys and the right subtree contains larger keys, enabling logarithmic search performance.
steps: Define a Node structure containing the SKU key, value, and pointers to left and right children.
Insert SKUs into the tree by recursively comparing the new key against the current node to determine the path.
Traverse the tree using in-order logic to maintain a sorted view of the inventory for reporting.
Implement a search function that branches left or right based on key comparison to locate specific items.
outcome: Faster retrieval of product availability data, reducing the time required to process individual customer orders.
limitation: The tree can become unbalanced if keys are inserted in sorted order, effectively turning it into a linked list; performance must be monitored by checking the tree height relative to the number of nodes.

questions.question: In Optimizing Inventory Lookup for Retail Logistics, why is a Binary Search Tree preferred over a flat list?
options: It enables logarithmic search performance by partitioning comparisons.
It eliminates the need for unique SKU identifiers.
It automatically reorders the entire warehouse floor.
It guarantees the fastest possible insertion regardless of key order.
questions.explanation: The solution explains that the BST structure enables logarithmic search performance by organizing SKUs into a hierarchy where subtrees partition comparisons.
questions.evidence: Implementing a Binary Search Tree (BST) organizes SKUs into a hierarchical structure where each node's left subtree contains smaller keys and the right subtree contains larger keys, enabling logarithmic search performance.

questions.question: What is a primary limitation of the implementation described in Optimizing Inventory Lookup for Retail Logistics?
options: The tree cannot store more than ten thousand items.
The tree can become unbalanced if keys are inserted in sorted order.
The search function requires a full traversal of all nodes.
The memory overhead of pointers exceeds the storage of the keys.
questions.explanation: The limitation section explicitly warns that sorted insertion can degrade the tree into a linked list, impacting performance.
